post.title: $15.9B in reported fraud losses. Is that charity real?
post.ig:
Americans reported losing $15.9 billion to fraud in 2025 (FTC).

Reported fraud losses: $3.3B in 2020 to $15.9B in 2025, as first reported by the FTC.
In September 2026, Hawaii's attorney general warned of fraudulent charities after Hurricane Lowell.
FTC red flags: pressure to give right now; cash, gift card, wire or crypto requests; names that sound like well-known charities.
From 2026, non-itemizers can deduct up to $1,000 ($2,000 married) in cash gifts, only to qualified charities. Example: $500 x 22% = $110 less tax; a fake charity gives $0.

Sources: FTC Consumer Sentinel; FTC consumer alert Aug 27, 2026; Hawaii Dept. of the Attorney General; IRS.
News and education, not financial advice.

FTC red flags include pressure to give right now, requests for cash, gift cards, wires or crypto, and copycat names. From 2026, non-itemizers can deduct up to $1,000 ($2,000 married) in cash gifts to qualified charities, which the IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search lists.
